steps.explanation: Replication in action: the helicase ring spins as it unzips the DNA, and the two DNA polymerases pull in new nucleotides one at a time.
Ahead of the fork, topoisomerase opens its gate to cut and rejoin the DNA, relieving the twisting built up by unwinding.
Helicase uses energy from ATP to move along the template, breaking the hydrogen bonds between the base pairs.
Single-strand binding proteins hold the separated strands apart so they don't pair up again.
Primase lays down a short RNA primer, giving DNA polymerase a place to start.
DNA polymerase adds matching nucleotides (A with T, G with C), building each new strand in the 5' to 3' direction.
On the leading strand, the new DNA is built continuously, towards the fork.
On the lagging strand, it is built in short Okazaki fragments, each starting from its own primer.
